title: Customize Pattern Annotation | Clo Feature Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our Annotation feature in CLO 2025.0 allows you to set the orientation, size, and color of pattern annotations for quick and clear access to pattern information. Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

summary: ```markdown # Customize Pattern Annotation | Clo Feature Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe and I'm going to go through our update to Annotations. This update was added for our 2025.0 release. So, let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Adding Annotations Here I have a pattern, and what I'm going to do is start adding some annotations. Adding annotations is really easy. All you have to do is go down here in your 2D toolbar. You're going to see a little tool that says "A." Then, you can click on it, click onto your pattern, and write in some annotations. For example: - Sleeve - Left - Cut one - Action ready - Top - 42 Once you're done typing, you can then go to another pattern, click on "front body," and proceed as needed. ## Updates to Annotation Tools There are some updates in which you can now do more than before. Previously, you could type in your annotations, hit enter, and go about your work. However, now when you open up the property editor, you will see your edit annotations tool right above the "A." It’s an "A" with a little cursor next to it. You can select this tool, and over in your profile, you can see this as a file. In your property editor, you can change: - Font size - Color - Angle For instance, you might want the annotation to be parallel with green, on the x-axis, or at a custom angle. You can do all of that! You can even double-click on an annotation to edit it. ## Editing Annotations If you want to rotate an annotation, you can right-click to delete it or copy it. You can also paste it if needed. Moreover, you can select it, right-click, and rotate clockwise by 45 degrees or reset it along the baseline. For shortcuts, you can hit `Ctrl + C` to copy and `Ctrl + V` to paste. After pasting, you might want to click on the annotation and say "back body." If you want to change the color of this annotation, you can easily do that as well. ## Conclusion There are a lot more editing capabilities with annotations, allowing you to provide more information on your patterns. This will enhance your workflow and make it easier to move your projects into production. Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe; there are a ton of great videos on our YouTube channel, so check that out. Thanks again for watching, and keep having fun in the club! ```
